title: ARIS /research-wiki + /meta-optimize — Self-Optimizing Research Knowledge Base
description: Two new skills added to the ARIS (Auto-Research-In-Sleep) framework in early April 2026: (1) /research-wiki (April 8): Persistent research knowledge base inspired by Karpathy's LLM Wiki. Accumulates papers, ideas, experiments, and claims across the full research lifecycle with typed relationships. Hooks integrate with /research-lit (paper intake), /idea-creator (reads wiki + writes ideas), and /result-to-claim (updates claim status + triggers re-ideation). Failed ideas become anti-repetition memory — ARIS learns from mistakes across sessions. (2) /meta-optimize (April 5): Outer-loop harness optimization. Passively logs skill invocations, tool calls, failures, and parameter overrides via Claude Code hooks. Running /meta-optimize analyzes usage data and proposes SKILL.md improvements — reviewed by a reviewer agent and approved by user. Inspired by Meta-Harness (Lee et al., 2026). ARIS can now optimize its own skill definitions. Framework also added Codex Plugin deep integration (April 4): /codex:rescue auto-invoked on experiment failure or LaTeX compilation failure.

matches: Instinct System / Continuous Learning v2 — behavioral learning from git-integrated evolution

redundancy_check.verdict: NOVEL — /research-wiki is domain-specific (ML research) with typed cross-session relationships and anti-repetition tracking not present in Context Librarian or Instinct System. /meta-optimize is a passive hook-based self-improvement system for SKILL.md files — different from DSPy prompt optimizer (which requires explicit metric/dataset setup, not passive usage logging).
redundancy_check.key_distinction: /research-wiki adds typed relationship tracking (paper→idea→experiment→claim) with failure memory. /meta-optimize uses Claude Code hooks to passively collect usage data and propose skill improvements — zero-configuration self-improvement loop not available in DSPy optimizer.

notes: ARIS framework is ML research-specific. The /research-wiki and /meta-optimize patterns have broader applicability beyond ML research: /research-wiki generalizes to any domain requiring cross-session typed knowledge accumulation; /meta-optimize generalizes to any Claude Code skill system. The /meta-optimize pattern is particularly interesting for the claude-evolution system — it could be applied to our own skill files. Skills are Markdown-only (no framework dependencies), cross-agent (works with Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenClaw). License not clearly stated on repo. Stars: not directly confirmed for main repo, but AAAI 2026 acceptance of paper produced using ARIS indicates academic validation.

evaluation.reasoning: ARIS framework is ML-research-centric, but /meta-optimize in particular has high applicability to the claude-evolution system (passive SKILL.md self-improvement via hooks). Integration complexity (55): requires installing skills and configuring passive hook logging in settings.json — moderate. Token efficiency (55): neutral to slight positive; /meta-optimize could reduce wasted tokens over time by improving skills, but /research-wiki adds context overhead. Capability expansion (65): /meta-optimize is incrementally interesting (hook-based passive logging + proposal generation is not replicated by DSPy optimizer); /research-wiki is domain-specific and less applicable. Maintenance burden (65): active ML research framework, monthly checks; ML-research-specific focus may drift from our use case. Community validation (55): AAAI 2026 paper acceptance = academic validation, but no confirmed GitHub star count — below 1k+ threshold. Research needed to determine if /meta-optimize is extractable as a standalone pattern for our skill system.
